finding: Let a=||A||F²,b=||B||F²,p=Tr[(A†A)²],q=Tr[(B†B)²],z=Re(conj(Tr A²) Tr B²), with traceless A,B∈M4(C). For X=A⊗I+I⊗B, exact expansion gives Tr[(X†X)²]=4(p+q)+4ab+2z and Tr(X†X)=4(a+b). Cauchy–Schwarz on the two largest nonnegative eigenvalues of X†X gives σ1(X)²+σ2(X)²≤sqrt(2 Tr[(X†X)²]). Therefore the full T2 dual holds whenever 2(p+q)+z≤a²+b²; strict inequality gives a strict positive dual gap unless X=0. This is a universal sufficient test in original A,B variables; not a source-conditional bound.
proof_details: Expand X†X=A†A⊗I+I⊗B†B+A†⊗B+A⊗B†. Mixed traces with the first two terms vanish because Tr A=Tr B=0; the cross-square contributes 2ab+2z. The Cauchy–Schwarz step is (s1+s2)²≤2(s1²+s2²)≤2 sum_j s_j² for eigenvalues s_j of X†X. Rearrangement of sqrt(2M)≤2(a+b) yields the displayed criterion exactly.
